approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves new molecular graphs from accepted molecules, fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process and an adapted native quantile model to the current session, and spends evaluations on sequential sampled maxima. Its native model keeps all fingerprint coordinates across eight views, including centered query values at coordinates constant in training. Each predicted quantile curve is centered at its own integrated mean and translated to the original GP mean. Correlated GP latent normals pass through those curves, while GP means control stalled-pool eligibility. Real accepted scores then update the archive, both models, survivors and breeding.
approach.novelty: This control removes only cross-candidate latent dependence by passing the existing independent normal coordinates directly through the unchanged native inverse quantiles. The correlated law remains a passive comparison on each actual pool. Recent siblings changed marginal shape or removed query-only input values; this intervention keeps both and preserves every univariate distribution. It tests whether dependence contributes to this composition, with earlier controls motivating the prediction that its removal will lower the endpoint.

observed_bottleneck: The adapted native-quantile Parent n-ada68e100737 converted more purchases into positive gain over actual generating parents (full 16.68612674725103), but late gain fell to 3.915646383849673 and mean endpoint 0.5622564516615843 (seed population SD 0.005481732549278124) remains 0.04477386454954668 below formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de. All fifteen Parent task cells across three summary/run pairs complete their issued budget; its analysis records 435 native allocations, 420 probes and no fallback. Thus the limiting behavior is poor conversion of the existing residual-guided purchases into sustained endpoint progress, while the conditional contribution of its cross-candidate dependence is unidentified. The shape sibling n-741da1149559 refutes its full-and-late gain conjunction; the zero-C sibling n-cfa00d1cee11 supports retaining nonzero query C with a -0.009829266306907688 removal delta. Neither isolates dependence. Earlier dependence controls n-5e03d3ccd1b7 and n-61819156f98f show removal losses on restricted Gaussian and qPO hosts, respectively. Those are contrary guidance for removing dependence, not evidence of its contribution under these nonlinear native marginals. This frozen validation ticket resolves that remaining consumer question without changing the established marginal host.

hypothesis: Remove only cross-candidate latent dependence at every successful allocation on the adapted native host. Keep the unchanged Q_i, integrated m_i, original GP location/mask and exact original normal tensor Z. Consume S_i=mu_GP_i+Q_i(Phi(Z_i))-m_i instead of mu_GP_i+Q_i(Phi((Z@F.T)_i/d_i))-m_i. Keep the full original factorization and jitter, draw count/order/shape, all marginal predictions/probes and the existing sequential availability/tie rule. The law has independent candidate coordinates before sequential selection and exactly the same one-dimensional bounded native marginals; finite empirical sample covariance need not be zero and selected choices remain dependent. Retain correlated transport as a passive same-state comparator using the same Z and Q, with no new inference or random draw. Do not alter amplitude, input columns, shape, mean, mask or within-batch conditioning.

finding_summary.headline: The dependence control changed purchases; a timeout leaves its contribution unresolved.
finding_summary.insights: This rules out a dormant control: the borrowed marginal/dependence separation and integrated-moment preservation both operated, changed purchases, and reached real subsequent fitting and breeding. It does not settle whether retaining correlation is materially beneficial under these native marginals. The negative two-seed difference is compatible with the registered prediction, but cannot substitute for the missing endpoint and feedback boundary; the result is an incomplete test, not a refuted mechanism or proof of a positive contribution. The literature supplies the construction, while bounded constant tails and the sequential molecular consumer limit transfer. Search still concentrates on related aromatic amide/imide and amine families. Decoration hopping expands to median heavy-atom counts of 57, 83 and 67, versus 53, 36 and 45.5 for the Parent, while smaller Parent structures can score higher. Together with repeated whole-fragment assemblies, this points to a proposal limitation that chemically controlled scaffold reconnections and contraction moves could address; it does not identify the timeout cause or prove that size mediates score. The rest of the native method and the wider approach remain open.
finding_summary.results: The independent law executed in all 430 observed allocations with unchanged native marginals, GP locations, masks and input host. It changed 416 paid sets, 2030 selection positions and 1175 purchased identities relative to the correlated law on the same states. Of 4300 accepted optimizer purchases, 4290 have Candidate feedback receipts and 4150 enter both next real fits; ten accepted molecules at the timeout boundary have scores but no observed feedback. Positive gain over actual generating parents totals 13.31469246, including 3.24124709 in the late half, versus the Parent's complete 16.68612675 and 3.91564638. Those Child totals are partial and do not replace the endpoint test. Fourteen endpoints completed, with seven gains and seven losses; decoration hopping in seed 1 timed out at 250 observations. The two completed seed macros average 0.55399706, with matched Parent delta -0.00737268 (seed deltas -0.00109968 and -0.01364567). The full three-seed mean and contribution verdict remain unavailable. The original formal target of 0.60903032 is not achieved by this incomplete panel.

molecular.headline: Aromatic heterocycles and bridged amines coexist with oversized assemblies, reactive heteroatom bonds and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: Assessment of n-a511fe4e5301 against published code Parent n-ada68e100737, restricted to frozen Search seeds 0, 1 and 2. All listed Child and Parent trajectories were read; no listed paths are missing. Coverage is not a complete Child evaluation or a complete paired panel: context.comparison.child_complete and paired_complete are false, with complete matched replicas only at seeds 0 and 2. The seed-1 deco_hop summary records a candidate Objective Session timeout after 250 observations; its 240 accepted optimizer molecules remain descriptive partial evidence, with no endpoint reconstruction. The other Child task cells contain 300 observations each; the Parent has all listed complete Search cells. The digest therefore contains 850 observations/820 optimizer records for deco_hop and 900/870 for each other task. Initial observations are separated from optimizer output. Across the digest, optimizer ring-closure rates are 0.9885 to 1.0 and aromatic-token rates 0.7828 to 0.9989, supporting rich ring/aromatic character; these are string indicators, not perceived ring or atom fractions. All task digests report zero explicit stereocentre and charged-string rates. The structures nevertheless include potentially stereogenic bridged and fused saturated rings and neutral basic amines; absence of charge notation does not establish absence of ionization. Most sessions explore derivatives of a few heteroaromatic amide/imide or amine families, with graph diversity from fusion, bridging, substitution and repeated-fragment joining. Moderate structural diversity reflects these distinct families and substantial local motif retention, not an acyclic collapse or uniformly broad medicinal chemistry. Many individual fragments are familiar, but N-halogen/N-sulfur substitutions, highly bridged connectivity and large repeated aromatic assemblies make synthetic plausibility questionable and overall drug-likeness weak. No synthetic routes, stability measurements, pharmacology, mechanism activation or chemical mediation were established. RDKit size and scaffold descriptors are deterministic readings of accepted optimizer trajectory SMILES, not additional oracle measurements. Exact input paths, hashes, byte-identical run-relative staging-copy mappings, per-cell denominators, summaries and descriptor definitions are preserved in policy/scratch/r0066-01-improve-L01/molecular/source_audit.json; the original immutable request is policy/requests/r0066-01-improve-L01-molecular-assess-d97f2488b3d4a6e3.json. Every cited SMILES below is an exact digest or trusted Child trajectory string. Parent comparisons describe the published trajectories without introducing uncitable Parent-only SMILES.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer records are almost entirely aromatic and all contain ring-closure digits. Their per-seed median heavy-atom counts are 25, 24 and 24. Seed 0 concentrates on substituted indoles/enamines, including an N-chloro aryl enamine; seed 2 on vinyl/methoxy indole carboxamides with pyridyl appendages and direct N-S substitution; seed 1 reaches a compact, highly bridged aza-polycycle carrying a benzyl N-hydroxyamide. That highest observed molecule has 24 heavy atoms and mixed aromatic/saturated ring character. The Parent likewise has compact indole/aryl-amide families and unusual N-Cl, N-O and N-S connections; these are persistent chemistry motifs rather than a new general capability shown by this Child.
liabilities: N-halogen and direct N-S bonds appear among attractive-scoring analogues and require chemical stability and synthetic-route scrutiny.
The top bridged aza-polycycle has potentially stereogenic centres but no specified stereochemistry; valid connectivity does not establish practical accessibility.
Large joined aromatic structures consume observations despite extremely small scores.
missing_features: A sustained set of simpler, chemically conventional alternatives preserving the compact polar/aromatic arrangement is not demonstrated among the quoted high-scoring families; the exact missing optimum cannot be inferred from these scores.
Explicit stereochemical alternatives are absent for the bridged high-scoring structures; whether the objective distinguishes them is unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 bridged N-hydroxyamide scores 0.49065338146265813, while its fluorinated analogue scores 0.4624615253670981. A seed-2 compact vinyl/methoxy N-S indole carboxamide scores 0.4369542269692598. At the opposite extreme, the 49-heavy-atom duplicated polyaromatic ether-linked structure scores 3.292559601310048e-19. The visible gradient is consistent with a compact heterocycle/amide arrangement and restrained size rather than extensive joining of aromatic fragments. It does not isolate any beneficial effect of N-O, N-S, halogenation or cage formation.

per_task.generated_character: The 820 accepted optimizer records include the censored seed-1 session. They are predominantly aromatic, branched assemblies of pyridyl/pyrrolyl or imide-containing fragments, connected through ketones, amides, thioesters, ethers and anhydride-like acyl-O-acyl links. Per-seed heavy-atom medians are 57, 83 and 67; maxima are 114, 120 and 120. The highest observed seed-2 structure has 107 heavy atoms and 11 RDKit aromatic rings, with repeated halogenated heteroaryl and tertiary-amide units. The seed-0 best instead has 59 heavy atoms, a nitrogen-rich aromatic core, thioesters and an N-chlorourea-like group. The partial seed-1 best has 83 heavy atoms and multiple repeated imide/fused-ring fragments. Published Parent medians are 53, 36 and 45.5; its best structures also show heteroaromatic/imide repetition but its seed-2 best has 52 heavy atoms. The observed size expansion is descriptive and cannot explain the timeout or attribute an algorithmic effect.
liabilities: Very large aromatic assemblies, numerous linkage choices and repeated polar fragments make practical synthesis and ordinary small-molecule developability doubtful.
Acyl-O-acyl linkages, thioesters, N-Cl bonds and chloromethyl substituents introduce potential reactivity or hydrolytic liabilities; these were not experimentally measured.
The low-scoring tail includes FBr and other tiny fragments that are not useful drug-like scaffold alternatives.
missing_features: Compact, chemically ordinary reconnections that retain useful fragment relationships are not consistently represented in the high-scoring Child structures; no exact required decoration or linker can be recovered from scalar scores alone.
A clear separation of new scaffold topology from simply repeating existing heteroaromatic/imide units is absent from the dominant large assemblies.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Tiny fragments such as ethene, diethyl ether and FBr score 0.5. The 107-heavy-atom assembly reaches 0.6019164728038108, but the much smaller 59-heavy-atom seed-0 structure reaches 0.6009364661021701. Thus the sampled score rewards some organized aromatic/polar fragment content over tiny fragments, but additional mass alone is not a demonstrated benefit. The authoritative Parent seed-2 best is 0.6324541616056452 at 52 heavy atoms, another counterexample to treating size growth as sufficient. The partial seed-1 maximum 0.587723380491437 at evaluation 248 remains an observed maximum, not a completed endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer records are rich in aromatic rings and halogens, with per-seed median heavy-atom counts of 29, 30 and 34. Higher-scoring molecules combine saturated basic nitrogen centres with aromatic hydrophobic regions: an N-propyl bridged bicyclic amine/biaryl in seed 0, an N-propyl azetidine attached to an amino-substituted diaryl ether ring system in seed 1, and a fused/bridged polyamine with a difluorophenylethyl appendage in seed 2. The latter two examples have 29 and 26 heavy atoms. The seed-1 leader also carries an aldehyde and a bromomethyl group. The Parent likewise produces aromatic/basic-amine combinations, ranging from a sulfoxide-containing amine to polycyclic or N-halogenated analogues. Basic amines are present; their absence is not this generator’s gap.
liabilities: The high-scoring aldehyde and bromomethyl groups introduce possible reactivity and metabolic liabilities.
Azetidine and densely bridged polyamine connectivity may be synthetically demanding, with unassigned stereochemistry at potential stereogenic centres.
Heavy halogen use is pervasive in the string counters, but neither selectivity nor developability was measured.
missing_features: Systematic lower-strain, less reactive analogues retaining the high-scoring amine/aromatic geometry are not established by the quoted leaders.
Defined stereoisomers and protonation-state comparisons are absent from the supplied output evidence; there is no demonstrated score requirement for a particular unobserved state.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aldehyde/bromomethyl azetidine structure scores 0.9947451017890969 and the bridged difluorophenylethyl polyamine 0.9946517216018368. The N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine bearing an N-chloro carboxamide scores only 0.00016650955053713697; its nitrogen is sulfonylated rather than an ordinary free basic amine. However, the much simpler aryl-substituted cyclic diamine alcohol also scores only 0.0025071411389405336. The association therefore concerns the arrangement of an amine, aromatic surfaces and ring topology, not mere nitrogen presence. These scores alone do not establish a binding pose, measured affinity or the benefit of the reactive substituents.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer records mainly form propyl/methyl-substituted aryl or aza-aryl rings linked to N-rich cyclic amide/imide systems and an ethoxyphenyl group. Per-seed median heavy-atom counts are 35, 35 and 34. The best seed-0 molecule has 35 heavy atoms, a diazine-like aromatic ring, an ethoxyphenyl group and a bridged N-methyl carbonyl-containing ring system; related seed-1 and seed-2 leaders retain these general appendages while changing fusion and saturation. The Parent similarly combines alkyl/ethoxy aromatic fragments with N-methyl carbonyl-containing rings. The Child therefore shows topology variation within retained fragment families rather than a newly demonstrated wide scaffold repertoire.
liabilities: Dense N-rich bridging, adjacent N-N connectivity in some analogues and multiple carbonyl-containing rings make synthetic feasibility less obvious than valid SMILES suggests.
Large joined derivatives and very small fragments both occur, without demonstrating a chemically balanced alternative family.
Potentially stereogenic ring junctions are left unspecified.
missing_features: Chemically simple scaffold alternatives preserving the useful aromatic substituent and carbonyl arrangement are not demonstrated as a broad high-scoring family.
Controlled stereochemical alternatives for the bridged carbonyl/amine systems are missing; scalar scores do not establish that stereochemistry would improve this objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The bridged seed-0 structure reaches 0.24470707585221768; related seed-1 and seed-2 best structures score 0.2369593480332035 and 0.23814483610392007. Methane and the small peroxide-containing OOCS structure score 0.0, while O=C(O)NO scores 0.008197822947299411. The visible gradient favours retention and arrangement of the larger aromatic/alkyl/carbonyl fragment combination over radical fragmentation. The modest changes among related leaders do not reveal which missing connectivity would resolve the remaining mismatch.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 optimizer records mostly retain cyclic urea/imide or related lactam motifs with fluorinated unsaturated carbocycles and N-rich heterocycles. Per-seed median heavy-atom counts are 28, 27 and 26. The seed-1 leader has 26 heavy atoms: a methylimidazole attached to a fused dicarbonyl N-heterocycle, with one N-methyl, one N-F and a methyl/fluorocyclopentadienyl substituent. The seed-0 leader is a more bridged, nonaromatic dicarbonyl polycycle with N-F and N-S bonds; the seed-2 leader has a hydroxylated N-methyl lactam and difluoroacetyl hydrazine-like substituent. The Parent also retains fluorinated carbocycles and N-methyl/N-F dicarbonyl heterocycles, although its seed-1 best uses an imino/oxo aza-heterocycle instead. These are seed-dependent related families, not one universal optimum.
liabilities: N-fluoro imide/amine and direct N-S bonds are unusual medicinal-chemistry endpoints and need stability and synthetic-route assessment.
Unsaturated fluorinated small rings and dense bridging can complicate accessibility; several potential stereocentres are unspecified.
Very large joined copies of the retained heterocycle motif appear despite extremely small scores.
missing_features: Broader conventional fluorinated polar scaffolds with simpler linkages are not demonstrated among the leaders, which repeatedly vary the inherited dicarbonyl ring family.
Stereochemically specified saturated alternatives are absent; the score evidence does not show that an unobserved amine or named reference scaffold is required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The methylimidazole/dicarbonyl leader scores 0.5665271676826751, and the related N-methyl analogue with a difluorinated unsaturated carbocycle scores 0.5571531874286334 without an N-F bond. The seed-0 bridged structure reaches 0.5183475680761325 and the seed-2 hydroxylated lactam 0.4996315649004825. A 48-heavy-atom duplicated dicarbonyl/aryl assembly scores 2.9279184409751896e-25. The gradient supports a compact fluorinated polar heterocycle arrangement over doubled architectures. It neither identifies a specific missing pharmacophore nor demonstrates that N-fluorination itself is rewarded.

transferable_gaps.evidence: In n-a511fe4e5301 Search trajectories, compact high-scoring families have roughly two dozen to mid-thirties heavy atoms, whereas a repeated heteroaromatic assembly reaches 107 heavy atoms and other accepted structures reach 120. In that same large-assembly family a 59-heavy-atom structure has nearly the same observed score. Published Parent n-ada68e100737 also supplies smaller related examples. These are within-session chemistry associations, with the incomplete seed-1 session preserved, not causal evidence about an algorithm component.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks consistent control of molecular size while retaining useful local fragment relationships.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide task-agnostic contractions and reconnections that preserve selected local fragments without repeatedly duplicating whole ring systems. Compare accepted outcomes within each session; neither impose a universal size optimum nor infer a benefit from molecular growth.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across n-a511fe4e5301 Search seeds, cited leaders include N-Cl enamines or urea-like groups, N-F carbonyl heterocycles and direct N-S bonds; other outputs include acyl-O-acyl links and bromomethyl groups. Related N-halogen motifs already occur in published Parent n-ada68e100737. A high-scoring N-methyl dicarbonyl analogue also exists without N-F, so reactive substitution is not established as necessary.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically conventional heteroatom bonding is not consistently retained during high-scoring structural exploration.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically ordinary heteroatom substitutions and stable linkage alternatives accessible alongside existing edits, using the same session feedback. Any chemical-prior intervention should be explicit and task-agnostic; graph validity and observed score must remain distinct from stability or synthesis evidence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest for n-a511fe4e5301 reports stereocentre_rate 0.0, while the trusted Search molecules include bridged aza-polycycles, substituted saturated ring junctions and asymmetric carbocyclic appendages. This describes output representation, not an established stereochemical score dependency or an inference about hidden generator internals.
transferable_gaps.gap: Explicit stereochemical exploration is absent despite repeated production of potentially stereogenic ring systems.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: If allowed within the existing molecular identity contract, generate stereochemically defined alternatives coherently when topology creates stereocentres, then let ordinary session evaluations determine whether they matter. Do not assume a preferred configuration or claim an improvement without observing it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The n-a511fe4e5301 Search outputs repeatedly return to indole/amide, dicarbonyl N-heterocycle and aromatic/basic-amine families; other graph variation comes from bridging, fusion or whole-fragment repetition. Tiny disconnected-in-purpose fragments score poorly in the cited sessions. Published Parent n-ada68e100737 shows related motif dependence. Diversity is moderate overall, not total collapse, and these observations do not identify the cause of local concentration.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful fragment retention is demonstrated more clearly than broad scaffold changes with chemically controlled connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Enable scaffold-changing moves that keep chosen local polar and aromatic relationships through chemically reasonable ring or linker alternatives. Assess whether new families actually enter accepted high-scoring output, without task identity, external answer motifs or component-attribution claims.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
